title: If posting a one shot post, should OP have to give the prompt out as proof?
author: Trashy_io
selftext: I just think this would be beneficial to cut down on fake hype post claiming to be a one shot and just in general as hopefully they see it as such a valuable skill they can keep it to themselves. Im just not here for the one shot hype, I like it and definitely has its use cases but not in a sub reddit where thats where most people started and is considered the bear minimum now. Just would like more serious discussion and project to be on the feed.

comments.author: mallcopsarebastards
comments.body:
no? 

For one thing, posting the prompt isn't evidence of anything. For another, you realize you can scroll past or downvote things you dont' like, right?

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I don’t really think it’s necessary. Even if the prompt works for you once, LLMs are not deterministic, and the same prompt may not give similar results. 

I don’t think one-shots are really that interesting anyway and I don’t see that many posts about them.

comments.author: robogame_dev
comments.body: It shouldn't be a server rule, but if they won't post their prompt its essentially meaningless...

comments.author: Jolva
comments.body: I don't understand the weird obsession with one shotting anything personally. It's neat to see what an AI can do in a single prompt I guess, but what's the point other than to show your friends/Reddit? Why not use six prompts and have all of the characters named after your friends or something?

replies.author: HippieYoHippieYay
replies.body:
Because a lot of people don't actually know what to do with AI, and have no real projects.

It's the equivalent of buying the best and most expensive photography gear, and then just end up taking pictures of their cat inside their bedroom.

comments.author: Nasdali
comments.body: One shots are fun, but the prompt matters less for them than the connectors and skills the model has access too. So I’d rather see people include that information rather than the prompts.

comments.author: Sleepnotdeading
comments.body: I’d rather they not post one shots at all.  That’s not game dev.  That’s a vending machine.

comments.author: SnuffleBag
comments.body:
I think it would be benecifial if people completely stopped sharing anything about one shot output. 

That's not gamedev, it's just ... low. effort. slop. The only praise you can give it is the kind of encouragement you give an infant doing something incredibly simple very poorly.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body: Yeah. Let’s see how AI does with multi shots. I want to be impressed with how far the tool was taken not with how fast it spits out a clone.

replies.author: No-Difference629
replies.body: Check out my page, I made a mordhau sword fighting game with earlier ai models than what we have current.

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: almost half a year ago? where have you been hibernating? Pretty cool results!

comments.author: Dont_Bring_Me_Down
comments.body:
You’re completely right about the one-shot hype posts, but there is a hypocrisy in this sub.   
  
People constantly say that they want 'serious discussion and projects,' but the moment someone posts a highly detailed, technical breakdown of their actual build experience, it gets downvoted or ignored.

People say they want "substance", but then they treat it like it’s spam.

If the goal is a sub with serious discussion, then the community should actually back it up by upvoting and engaging with the deep dives, instead of burying the developers who are actually doing the heavy lifting.

Just a thought...

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: Yeah you might be right maybe we are the majority on this one as most people have already been sold the game developer dream thinking that effort is a non requirement now.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
I posted something like that. I explained in detail that it was still in development.

1.2k views on the post and not one single like or comment. 

I've made 328 commits on GitHub across 8 branches. Used more than 20 million Claude Pro tokens in less than a month.
I estimate around 1000 prompts using Claude code and OpenCode. I've used Opus, Sonnet and Fable, plus some free model use on OpenCode.

I have many months of development to go and without AI this would be impossible for me to do. It's hard even with AI, to come up with the game mechanics and the puzzles.

replies.author: brother_spirit
replies.body: I'll check you out. Got a web hosted demo I can play?

replies.author: CertainBlue
replies.body: that's just the nature of social networks, it's much easier to get attention posting something flashy rather than aiming for nuance

comments.author: OldManActual
comments.body:
Mods should deny those posts unless they come complete. I propose that all “look at my cool thing “ needs to follow a format and require the prompt,   an acceptable summary of what the user did and a link to a repo. Failing any of these the post is rejected. 

Useful products and research please. We are past the flex phase and the thinly veiled ads are bleh.

comments.author: AnimalPowers
comments.body: one shot isn’t impressive it’s just spam and shows low general comprehension capability

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
most people do but it is not required. there is no point lying about it unless they work for the AI company. 

I mean, we see those posts whenever GPT/Claude get a new update.

it has its values the baseline performance i.e. if your workflow is taking more time and you are not even meeting the quality of a one-shot game, you may as well evaluate your workflow

I personally pay attention to those posts as a way to keep up with the AI model updates without doing the prompting myself

comments.author: tyro12
comments.body: I think one shot people are regards. It's a worthless utterly stupid and meaningless metric to go by.

comments.author: poponis
comments.body: Honestly, one shot post should be not welcome in this redit. One shot is not game development.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: prompts mean little, llms are non deterministic so there is variablity, then you include custom agents, skills and other stuff, one prompt for one person will be something different. You would need aleast all of this to replciate
